description: Adversarial fault injection and cross-domain scenario execution matrix.

scenarios.name: Cross-Tenant Same-ID Collision
scenarios.injected_fault: Identical transaction_id 'tx_shared_001' ingested concurrently by Bank A and Bank B with conflicting amounts and accounts.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Partitioned tenant key set disjointness: set(Bank A keys) & set(Bank B keys) == empty_set; retry(Bank A) does not alter Bank B state.
scenarios.expected_result: Both transactions coexist in separate tenant namespaces; feature stores, graph edges, alerts, and cases remain strictly tenant-scoped.

scenarios.name: Same Event Redelivery
scenarios.injected_fault: Canonical transaction T redelivered 3 times through streaming ingestion simulating Kafka at-least-once transport retries.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Count of unique transactions in database == 1; count of edges in graph == 1; feature store customer history length == 1; webhook event_id is identical across dispatches.
scenarios.expected_result: Exact metamorphic state equivalence between single delivery [T] and triple delivery [T, T, T]. No duplicate graph edges, feature velocity increments, or persisted rows.

scenarios.name: Parallel Legitimate Transactions
scenarios.injected_fault: Two rapid legitimate transactions T1 and T2 executed between identical source and destination accounts with distinct transaction IDs.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Unique transaction set size == 2; MultiDiGraph edge count == 2; node degrees for sender and receiver == 2; neither transaction suppressed.
scenarios.expected_result: MultiDiGraph preserves both distinct parallel financial edges; velocity rules accurately count both events.

scenarios.name: Crash-Window Redelivery
scenarios.injected_fault: Transaction T mutation succeeds in graph/feature store, then broker/process crashes before offset acknowledgement; broker redelivers T.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Post-redelivery graph edge count == pre-crash edge count; feature velocity is not double-incremented; webhook event identity remains deterministic.
scenarios.expected_result: System absorbs crash-window redelivery with zero duplicate side effects. Duplicate transport attempt is safely distinguished from duplicate business entity.

scenarios.name: Concurrent Case Decision
scenarios.injected_fault: Two independent investigators load Case V1; Investigator A commits terminal closure to V2; Investigator B concurrently submits decision based on stale V1.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Investigator A commit succeeds (status updated, version incremented, timeline hash updated); Investigator B receives HTTP 409 Precondition Failed; no lost update.
scenarios.expected_result: Optimistic lock prevents stale overwrite; timeline integrity hash remains valid; audit log captures failed conflict attempt.

scenarios.name: Decision Provenance Under Async Activity
scenarios.injected_fault: High-risk transaction T and low-risk transaction U processed concurrently with randomized async execution interleaving and delayed explanation completion.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Direct mapping verification: response_T.transaction_id == T.id and response_T.alert.id == alert_T.id; response_U receives no attributes from T.
scenarios.expected_result: Zero cross-talk between concurrent async coroutines. Model score, SHAP attributions, alert details, and timeline remain strictly bound to respective transactions.

scenarios.name: Active Privacy / Robustness Path Truth
scenarios.injected_fault: 1. Configuration enabling DP executes actual clipping and noise addition. 2. Configuration with Byzantine defense executes robust aggregator. 3. Incompatible configuration (SecAgg + non-linear Krum defense) injected.
scenarios.independent_oracle: DP runtime path records non-zero spent epsilon; robust defense filters out poisoned weights; incompatible SecAgg + Krum pipeline raises InvalidPipelineConfigurationError upfront.
scenarios.expected_result: Security/privacy controls are executed for real; invalid composition is rejected rather than silently downgraded.

scenarios.name: Failure Propagation
scenarios.injected_fault: Injected failures across four boundaries: 1. Model inference forward pass raises RuntimeError. 2. Persistence commit fails. 3. Case CAS version mismatch. 4. Webhook HTTP dispatch timeout.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Inference failure returns HTTP 500 (not fallback 200); persistence failure aborts transaction; stale case mutation returns HTTP 409; webhook timeout returns False (not marked delivered).
scenarios.expected_result: Failures propagate truthfully across all layers. Zero conversion of failures into plausible false successes.

scenarios.name: Historical Decision Boundary
scenarios.injected_fault: Transactions ingested at T; baseline historical query executed with as_of=T; future high-value transaction added at T+1 hour; historical query re-executed with as_of=T.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Graph topology and edge count for as_of=T query before and after T+1 ingestion are mathematically identical. Future edge at T+1 is excluded from as_of=T evaluation.
scenarios.expected_result: Future events do not leak into historical point-in-time graph queries. Temporal event-time boundary is strictly preserved.

scenarios.name: Machine Result vs Human Outcome
scenarios.injected_fault: High-risk transaction triggers alert and case; case is formally resolved by compliance team as CLOSED_FALSE_POSITIVE under Four-Eyes dual control.
scenarios.independent_oracle: Historical alert risk score, model prediction, and explanation remain unchanged; case status reflects CLOSED_FALSE_POSITIVE; SAR report generation is rejected with HTTP 400.
scenarios.expected_result: Human clearance does not rewrite or erase machine prediction history. Regulatory filing eligibility reflects false-positive clearance truthfully.
